ASI Ranjeet Singh, Police Station Dharampur, District Solan, H.P., present in person alongwith record.

The petitioner seeks regular bail in FIR No.22/2023, dated 26.03.2023, registered under Sections 21 and 29 of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985 (in short 'NDPS Act') and Section 181 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 at Police Station Dharampur, District Solan, H.P.

sentences.text: The respondent has filed the status report and also produced the record.

3. Facts:-
3(i).

As per the status report, on 26.03.2023, a police .
party was on patrol duty.
At about 5:50 pm, a confidential information was received that a vehicle as described in the information was coming from Timber Trail Parwanoo and proceeding towards Solan.

The information was also to the of effect that the vehicle had three occupants carrying heroin and that search of the vehicle at that point of time could rt result in recovery of huge quantity of the contraband.
Information was treated as reliable.
Provisions of Section 42(2) of the NDPS Act were complied with.
Search party was duly constituted.
It proceeded on the spot described in the information.

On noticing the vehicle indicated in the information,
the same was signalled to stop.
The vehicle had three occupants.
The person sitting on the driver seat disclosed his name as Ravi Sharma (petitioner).
The lady sitting on the adjoining seat gave her name as Priya, whereas the person occupying the back seat gave his name as Nishant Thakur.
During search of the vehicle carried out in accordance with law, a plastic pouch kept in the dashboard was found, from which heroin weighing 16 grams was recovered.
The recovery led to registration of the FIR and arrest of all three occupants of the vehicle.
3(iii).

During investigations, petitioner statedly disclosed that he was habitual of consuming heroin since .
the year 2014.
He was a Taxi Driver and used to procure heroin from Chandigarh/Delhi/Manali as and when he visited these places.

He is further stated to have disclosed having known co-accused Nishant Thakur and Priya for of about 3-4 years and that on 26.03.2023, he alongwith the co-accused persons had gone to Manimajra in a vehicle rt belonging to father of the co-accused Nishant Thakur.
That he (petitioner) procured 16 grams of heroin from a person in Manimajra on paying Rs.35,000/- in cash, out of which Rs.15,000/- were contributed by the co-accused persons.
On their return journey to Shimla, their vehicle was intercepted by the police, which led to recovery of the contraband and registration of the FIR.
As per the status report, the co-accused persons have also confirmed the above narration of events in the investigations carried out by the respondent from them.

According to the respondent, the petitioner was taken to the spot disclosed by him for identifying the person from whom the contraband was statedly procured, however,
the said person could not be identified.

sentences.text: Learned Senior Counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner is behind the bars for past more than seven months.
Investigation in the matter is complete.

The charge-sheet has been filed by the .
respondent.
The guilt, if any, of the petitioner is yet to be proved.
Co-accused persons have already been released on bail.
Hence, prayer was made for enlarging the petitioner on bail.
Learned counsel further stated that the petitioner will of abide by all the terms and conditions, which may be imposed upon him in case of his enlargement on bail.
rt Learned Deputy Advocate General opposed the grant of bail and submitted that the petitioner has been accused of possessing 16 grams of heroin.
The respondent has enough evidence to proceed against him.

It was also submitted that the petitioner has criminal history inasmuch as five FIRs have been registered against him in different police stations, out of which, three are under the provisions of the NDPS Act and the other two are under different provisions of the Indian Penal Code.
5. The quantity of the contraband involved in the FIR in question is 16 grams of heroin, which falls in the 'intermediate category' under the NDPS Act.
Co-accused persons have already been enlarged on bail vide order dated 19.06.2023 passed in Cr.MP(M) Nos.1245 and 1246 of 2023.
The petitioner has already spent a period of more than seven months in custody.

The respondent has given the following criminal history of the petitioner:-
"1. FIR No.114/2019, dated 18.05.2019, under .
Sections 21 and 29 of the NDPS Act at Police Station Sadar, District Solan, H.P.
2. FIR No.56/2020, dated 23.09.2020, under Sections 21 and 29 of the NDPS Act at Police Station Kotkhai, District Shimla, H.P. of 3.
FIR No.106/2020, dated 20.10.2020, under Section 21 of the NDPS Act at Police Station Chotta Shimla, District Shimla, H.P.

4. rt FIR No.109/2014, dated 31.07.2014, under Sections 363, 366, 376, 342, 506 and 120B of the Indian Penal Code at Police Station Dhalli, District Shimla, H.P.
5. FIR No.121/2014, dated 18.08.2014, under Sections 279 and 323 of the Indian Penal Code at Police Station Dhalli, District Shimla, H.P.

"
However, learned Senior Counsel for the petitioner submitted that FIR No.109/2014
has since been quashed and the petitioner has been acquitted in FIR No.121 of 2014
. It was also submitted that FIR Nos.56/2020
pertain to petitioner's alleged possession of '5 grams' and '1 gram' of heroin, respectively.
FIR No.114/2019 pertains to alleged possession of 25.33 grams of heroin by the petitioner.

sentences.text:
The quantity of the contraband involved in the FIR in question, being intermediate, does not attract the .
provisions of Section 37 of the NDPS Act.
Guilt, if any, of the petitioner is yet to be proved during trial, which may take long time to conclude.
Petitioner is a local resident, therefore, his presence can be secured in the trial.
There is of no apprehension of his fleeing from justice.
The co-accused persons have already been enlarged on bail.
Petitioner by rt now has completed more than seven months in custody.
Charge-sheet has been filed by the respondent on 25.05.2023.
In the facts and circumstances of the case, further detention of the petitioner is not warranted.
Accordingly, the present petition is allowed.

The petitioner is ordered to be released on bail in the aforesaid FIR on his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- with one local surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the learned Trial Court having jurisdiction over the concerned Police Station, subject to the following conditions:-
(i). Petitioner is directed to join the investigation of the case as and when called for by the Investigating Officer in accordance with law.
(ii). Petitioner shall not tamper with the evidence or hamper the investigation in any manner whatsoever.
(iii). Petitioner will not leave India without prior permission of the Court.

. 
(iv). Petitioner shall not make any inducement, threat or promise, directly or indirectly, to the Investigating Officer or any person acquainted with the facts of the case to dissuade him/her from disclosing such facts to the Court or any Police Officer.
of (v).
In case of launching of prosecution, petitioner shall attend the trial on every hearing, unless exempted in accordance with law.
(vi). Petitioner shall inform the Station House Officer rt of the concerned police station about his place of residence during bail and trial.
Any change in the same shall also be communicated within two weeks thereafter.
Petitioner shall furnish details of his Aadhar Card, Telephone Number, E-mail, PAN Card, Bank Account Number, if any.
(vii).
It is made clear that in case petitioner is arraigned as an accused, in future, in any FIR under NDPS Act, then this bail is liable to be cancelled.
